title: Build a bounded byte ring
description: Implement the Ring functions declared in ring.h.
prompt:
Implement the Ring functions declared in ring.h.
The ring stores exactly four bytes in FIFO order. push returns 0 when full without modifying the queue. pop returns 0 when empty and leaves out unchanged. init resets the queue. This exercise is single-threaded; the tests do not establish ISR safety.
constraints: Use the provided struct without dynamic allocation.
Return 1 on a successful push or pop.

tests.name: FIFO order
Empty leaves output intact
Full rejects new byte
Repeated wrap

rubric: Respect the stated contract and bounds.
Explain integer widths, ownership, and relevant edge cases.
Separate host-test evidence from hardware guarantees.
follow_ups: Which state is shared by an ISR producer and a task consumer?
How could separate producer and consumer indices avoid a shared count?
How would you measure and report overflow under burst traffic?
hints: Write down the boundary cases before choosing an implementation.
Use explicit integer widths and keep intermediate values in range.
